title: Zuriel Chapter Introductions — 2 Samuel 13–24 (Part 2)
description: Chapter-by-chapter studies of David's family crisis, rebellion, restoration, songs, final words, and the closing account of his reign.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 13 — Amnon assaults Tamar
chapters.historicalContext: Amnon deceives and sexually assaults Tamar, then rejects her. Absalom takes her into his care, while David is angry but fails to bring justice.
chapters.overview: Amnon deceives and sexually assaults Tamar, then rejects her. Absalom takes her into his care, while David is angry but fails to bring justice.
chapters.studyObservation: The chapter exposes sexual violence, betrayal, silencing, and the failure of royal family protection.
chapters.connectionNotes: This chapter belongs to the closing movement of 2 Samuel; read it in sequence with chapters 12 and 14 to follow the consequences and transitions.
studyQuestions: What events and choices shape this chapter?
Whose perspective or experience needs careful attention?
What does the chapter reveal about power, justice, or faithfulness?
chapters.lifeApplication: Seek truth, protect the vulnerable, welcome accountability, and consider the consequences of leadership decisions.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: Tamar is not responsible for the assault. Never use this chapter to excuse sexual violence or silence victims.
chapters.readingNote: Read the chapter in its historical and literary setting, paying attention to the people affected by the events.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 14 — Absalom's revenge and flight
chapters.historicalContext: Absalom arranges Amnon's killing and flees to Geshur. David mourns, and the royal family remains fractured.
chapters.overview: Absalom arranges Amnon's killing and flees to Geshur. David mourns, and the royal family remains fractured.
chapters.studyObservation: The account shows how unaddressed violence and delayed justice can deepen family trauma and lead to further harm.
chapters.connectionNotes: This chapter belongs to the closing movement of 2 Samuel; read it in sequence with chapters 13 and 15 to follow the consequences and transitions.
studyQuestions: What events and choices shape this chapter?
Whose perspective or experience needs careful attention?
What does the chapter reveal about power, justice, or faithfulness?
chapters.lifeApplication: Seek truth, protect the vulnerable, welcome accountability, and consider the consequences of leadership decisions.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: Absalom's revenge is narrated, not commended; private vengeance is not a model of justice.
chapters.readingNote: Read the chapter in its historical and literary setting, paying attention to the people affected by the events.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 15 — Absalom's conspiracy and David's flight
chapters.historicalContext: Absalom wins public favour through calculated gestures and declares himself king at Hebron. David leaves Jerusalem as rebellion grows.
chapters.overview: Absalom wins public favour through calculated gestures and declares himself king at Hebron. David leaves Jerusalem as rebellion grows.
chapters.studyObservation: Political manipulation and unresolved grievance destabilize the kingdom.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 16 — David flees; Ziba, Shimei, and rival counsel
chapters.historicalContext: David leaves the city, sends the ark back, and receives loyal support. Shimei curses him; Absalom enters Jerusalem and hears competing counsel.
chapters.overview: David leaves the city, sends the ark back, and receives loyal support. Shimei curses him; Absalom enters Jerusalem and hears competing counsel.
chapters.studyObservation: The chapter contrasts loyalty, strategy, worship, insult, and the painful cost of civil conflict.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 18 — Absalom defeated and killed
chapters.historicalContext: David's forces defeat Absalom's army. Joab kills Absalom despite David's instruction to deal gently with him, and David grieves.
